newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MINING CHAMBER UPBEAT ON INDUSTRY FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MINING CHAMBER UPBEAT ON INDUSTRY FUTURE.

text.p: South Africa's mining chamber said on Tuesday the country will stay one of the world's great gold producers if mining firms remain innovative, entrepreneurial and tough-minded.

Bobby Godsell, the vice-president of the Chamber of Mines, told a conference in Toronto that the squeeze on margins seen at South African gold mines over the past 15 years could be reversed despite a continued fall in production.

Godsell, who is also chief executive of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's gold arm Anglogold, said in a statement three factors suggest that the industry would continue to be profitable and globally competitive into the next century. These were:
* a growing recognition at both the political and industrial relations levels of the urgent need to make the industry globally competitive;
* an improvement in both operational efficiency and labour productivity; and
* the existence of pilot projects at all mining groups demonstrating the dramatic extent of productivity gains.

"Although the industry is still in the early stages of this productivity renaissance, evidence is mounting that it is possible to mine gold in South Africa at present grades and in the present deep level circumstances at costs which are globally competitive," Godsell said.

South African gold production, hit by a combination of physical ore depletion, declining average grade and the higher costs associated with mining at deeper levels, last year fell to its lowest level in 40 years sliding to 494.62 tonnes.

In a bid to increase resources firms are pushing mines deeper with gold already being procured from around 3.7 km below ground. Anglo's Western Deep Levels Ltd mine has started a project which will extend its mining reach to nearly four kilometres underground.
